When I started tech, it wasn’t really because I was passionate about tech.

I was tired of the traditional way of working. The corporate way of working that takes so much of your time, effort, and even your youth, and sometimes still doesn’t give you enough in return.

And honestly, in the beginning, I was LOST.

You learn a skill and they tell you, try Upwork, try Fiverr, try this, try that.

Meanwhile, you see people on LinkedIn talking about how they’re getting jobs, landing contracts, building careers, and doing so well.

And I kept asking myself, how are these people actually doing this?

I asked people.

I asked people who were already doing the things I wanted to do. I asked how they were getting jobs. I asked how they were finding opportunities. I asked how they were navigating everything.

And most of the time, I got nothing.

Nobody really wanted to tell you.

I remember meeting people who had completely changed their careers. One person started as a Virtual Assistant, took a data analytics course, and eventually became a Project Manager.

So I kept learning too. I learned IT skills. I learned project management. I tried different things.

But project management wasn’t what I wanted to do.

Maybe because I had been a teacher for so many years, I was naturally drawn to people. Talking to people. Helping people. Solving problems. That was where I found myself.

So I kept asking.

Eventually, someone told me to use the internet.

And I thought, okay, but how do I do it exactly?

Because at the time, I would go to Google and type things like Virtual Assistant jobs or Customer Support jobs and get loads of generic nonsense.

Fill this form.

Click this link.

Submit here.

Then another email.

Then another form.

And the tunnel just kept going.

At the end, you’re left wondering, how are these people actually getting jobs?

Because if this is where everyone is finding opportunities, then what am I missing?

So one day, I decided to go to AI and ask.

I explained that so many people had told me to use the internet to find jobs, but nobody had actually explained how to do it.

And AI gave me a breakdown of exactly what to search for and how to search for it.

I started applying those search techniques.

And suddenly, I started finding actual leads.

Now, when I’m looking for Customer Success opportunities, for example, I don’t just search Customer Success jobs.

I’ll search for things like customer support agencies hiring, customer success agencies hiring, companies looking for customer experience teams, and other specific searches that lead me to actual opportunities.

And the difference is HUGE.

I’m finding leads that actually make sense. Opportunities where you’re filling out a real application instead of entering an endless tunnel of generic forms.

That experience taught me something:

ASK QUESTIONS.

Please, ask questions.

Ask people who are doing what you want to do.

Ask how they got there.

Ask what they searched.

Ask what resources they used.

Ask what you’re missing.

The worst thing that can happen is that someone tells you no.

But also, don’t make asking people your only strategy.

Use the resources around you.

Google.

AI.

YouTube.

Communities.

People who are willing to teach.

And speaking of people who are willing to teach, I’m genuinely grateful for people like @iamrichygold here.

This guy has been pouring out so much knowledge for free.

Knowledge that people would naturally charge you for.

And I try as much as possible to repost his content because I genuinely believe that when someone is willing to share useful information freely, it deserves to reach more people.

So yes, ask questions.

But also learn how to find answers for yourself.

Because sometimes the problem isn’t that there are no jobs.

Sometimes, you simply haven’t learned how to find them yet.

Prompt for AI video generation (Runway / Kling / Luma / Hailuo / etc.)

A vertical 9:16 cinematic AI art video, 10 seconds long, smooth continuous morphing transformation of a hyper-detailed surreal fashion portrait of a beautiful woman.

The face is always split vertically down the middle: left side porcelain-white skin with icy blue eyes and glossy red lips, right side deep matte black skin with glowing red eyes and metallic silver lips. High-fashion editorial beauty, sharp features, intense gaze looking straight at camera.

Throughout the video the face constantly shatters and recomposes with floating geometric fragments: sharp white and black triangular shards, cracked porcelain pieces, paper-like geometric planes, and bold red triangular cutouts that slide across the eyes, cheek, and lips. Large delicate white flowers (cosmos/peony style) bloom and dissolve over the head and face. A small delicate white bird occasionally appears perched on a flower or flying across the composition. Soft smoke and abstract black-and-white fabric shapes swirl around.

Sequence of elegant morphs:
- Start with cracked geometric glasses and floating white cubes
- Transition into flower-crowned face with bird and shattered glass
- Minimalist black/white face with pure white triangles
- Bold red geometric cutouts over the mouth and cheek
- Full floral headdress with bird and red triangle accent
- Abstract fragmented flower-covered face with single red eye
- Cracked flower-over-face composition with flying bird
- Dualistic face with black/white flowers and red diagonal slash
- Final intense geometric shatter with red triangles and floating petals

Ultra-detailed skin texture, dramatic high-contrast lighting, dark abstract background, cinematic depth of field, smooth slow morphing animation, dreamlike and elegant, no text, no watermark.

**Music / audio:**
Dark elegant ethereal ambient track — soft melancholic piano, subtle low strings, atmospheric pads, and delicate glassy textures. Mysterious, sophisticated, slightly haunting mood that perfectly matches the black/white dualism and red accents. Soft dynamic swells that follow the morphing transformations. No vocals, high-quality stereo, cinematic and intimate.

Local AI is exploding!

Transformers.js, that we've been building @huggingface for the past three years has now become the most popular open-source library to run AI models directly in your browser and crossed 10 million (!!) monthly downloads, close to 10x from just six months ago.

More generally, I'm excited to see a meaningful percentage of AI workloads move to local because it's free & fully private! At a time of compute shortage & increased cyber-attack risks, we need it more than ever.

Let's go!
